correctness.rationale: In the complex full flag case the boundary divisors at the Bruhat coatoms freely generate the Weil class group. The Picard basis is indexed by the simple support; the Chevalley coefficients in the divisor basis are the simple-coroot coordinates of the positive coroots of the right reflections giving the covers. The resulting integer map is injective. A Weil class has a positive multiple Cartier exactly when its image in the quotient is torsion, so Q-factoriality is finiteness of the cokernel, equivalently equality of the two basis ranks. Independently generated permutations of the 48 Euclidean F4 roots with the stated Cartan convention, length by positive-root inversions, support by membership in the four standard maximal parabolic subgroups, and covers via all 24 positive-root reflections. Exact Smith reduction gave full column rank, 6,168 covers across 1,152 elements, 919 positive-free-rank cokernels and finite types 0:171, Z/2:49, (Z/2)^2:13. Both witnesses' matrices agree up to row order; minimum lengths are 3 and 6. The index-two assertion follows from the exponent, not the maximum order.
residual_risks: No claim about torsion in the positive-rank quotients, local class groups, or parabolic flag varieties.
